review_locator: PMCID:PMC3396424, The Chemokine Superfamily Revisited; PMCID:PMC10157204, New pairings and deorphanization among the atypical chemokine receptor family
primary_title: Structure-function analysis of the extracellular domains of the Duffy antigen/receptor for chemokines: characterization of antibody and chemokine binding sites
decision_basis: The reviews identify DARC/ACKR1 as a multispecific chemokine-binding receptor; the cited primary study maps extracellular-domain residues required for CXCL8/IL-8 binding.
limitations_preserved: Binding-only atypical-receptor evidence; do not infer G-protein signaling or a CNS/SCI branch.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3396424, The Chemokine Superfamily Revisited; PMCID:PMC6120486, A guide to chemokines and their receptors
primary_title: Cutting edge: the orphan chemokine receptor G protein-coupled receptor-2 (GPR-2, CCR10) binds the skin-associated chemokine CCL27 (CTACK/ALP/ILC)
decision_basis: The reviews identify CCL27 as the skin-associated CCR10 ligand; the cited primary study shows CCL27 binding, calcium flux, and chemotaxis in CCR10/GPR2 transfectants, with in vivo skin-recruitment support.
limitations_preserved: Preserve skin-homing and ligand-presentation context; no CNS/SCI transfer.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5755716, CCL28 chemokine: An anchoring point bridging innate and adaptive immunity; PMCID:PMC6120486, A guide to chemokines and their receptors
primary_title: CCL28 has dual roles in mucosal immunity as a chemokine with broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity
decision_basis: The reviews identify CCR3 as a second CCL28 receptor; the cited primary studies show CCL28-responsive CCR3-positive mucosal/plasma-cell systems and CCR3/CCR10-dependent mucosal function.
limitations_preserved: Preserve shared CCR10/CCR3 usage and mucosal cell context; no purified-affinity or CNS/SCI overclaim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3396424, The Chemokine Superfamily Revisited; PMCID:PMC6120486, A guide to chemokines and their receptors
primary_title: Monocyte chemotactic protein-2 (MCP-2) uses CCR1 and CCR2B as its functional receptors
decision_basis: The reviews identify CCL8/MCP-2 among CCR1 ligands; the cited primary study demonstrates radioligand binding and migration through CCR1-transfected cells.
limitations_preserved: Preserve human CCL8 and CCR1/CCR2 promiscuity; no CNS/SCI transfer.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3396424, The Chemokine Superfamily Revisited; PMCID:PMC6120486, A guide to chemokines and their receptors
primary_title: Monocyte chemotactic protein-2 (MCP-2) uses CCR1 and CCR2B as its functional receptors
decision_basis: The reviews identify CCL8/MCP-2 among CCR2 ligands; the cited primary study demonstrates radioligand binding and migration through CCR2B-transfected cells.
limitations_preserved: Use human CCL8 with the CCR2B isoform boundary; do not infer mouse Ccl8 equivalence or CNS/SCI function.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3396424, The Chemokine Superfamily Revisited; PMCID:PMC6120486, A guide to chemokines and their receptors
primary_title: Monocyte chemoattractant protein-2 inhibits replication of HIV-1 via CCR5
decision_basis: The reviews identify CCL8/MCP-2 as a CCR5 ligand; the cited primary studies show CCR5-dependent calcium flux, cross-desensitization, and CCR5-transfectant signaling.
limitations_preserved: Preserve human ligand/receptor and shared-chemokine context; no CNS/SCI transfer.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6120486, A guide to chemokines and their receptors; PMCID:PMC7072521, Chemokines and their Receptors in Cancer Progression
primary_title: Functional expression of CCL8 and its interaction with chemokine receptor CCR3
decision_basis: The reviews identify CCL8 among promiscuous CC-receptor ligands; the cited primary study reports purified CCL8 binding to CCR3, receptor internalization, and weaker CCR3-cell chemotaxis.
limitations_preserved: Retain weaker/low-affinity CCR3 activity and recombinant/heterologous assay boundary; no CNS/SCI transfer.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3396424, The Chemokine Superfamily Revisited; PMCID:PMC6120486, A guide to chemokines and their receptors

decision_basis: The reviews identify CCL16/LEC as a multi-receptor chemokine; cited primary studies show CCR1 binding, chemotaxis, and Gi/Go-PLC-PKC signaling.
limitations_preserved: Preserve human CCL16 and low-affinity/multi-receptor caveat; no CNS/SCI transfer.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3396424, The Chemokine Superfamily Revisited; PMCID:PMC6120486, A guide to chemokines and their receptors
primary_title: Human CC chemokine liver-expressed chemokine/CCL16 is a functional ligand for CCR1, CCR2 and CCR5
decision_basis: The reviews identify CCL16/LEC as a CCR2 ligand; the cited primary study shows CCR2-dependent calcium mobilization and chemotaxis with direct low-affinity binding.
limitations_preserved: Preserve low-affinity and human ligand/receptor boundaries; no CNS/SCI transfer.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3396424, The Chemokine Superfamily Revisited; PMCID:PMC6120486, A guide to chemokines and their receptors
primary_title: Human CC chemokine liver-expressed chemokine/CCL16 is a functional ligand for CCR1, CCR2 and CCR5
decision_basis: The reviews identify CCL16/LEC as a CCR5-binding chemokine; the cited primary study shows low-affinity binding and calcium mobilization with marginal chemotaxis through CCR5.
limitations_preserved: Retain low-affinity/marginal-chemotaxis caveat; do not infer dominant CCR5 signaling or CNS/SCI function.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11115847, Structure and function of interleukin-22 and other members of the interleukin-10 family; PMCID:PMC2637415, Structure of IL-22 bound to its high-affinity IL-22R1 chain
primary_title: Structure of IL-22 bound to its high-affinity IL-22R1 chain
decision_basis: The reviews identify IL-22R1/IL22RA1 as the high-affinity ligand-specific chain; the cited primary study solves the IL-22/IL-22R1 extracellular complex and maps the binding interface.
limitations_preserved: Binary high-affinity binding only; IL10RB is a separate common co-receptor and no complete cell-surface relay is inferred from this row.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11115847, Structure and function of interleukin-22 and other members of the interleukin-10 family; PMCID:PMC2879597, Structure and mechanism of receptor sharing by the IL-10R2 common chain
primary_title: Comparison of interleukin-22 and IL-10 soluble receptor complexes
decision_basis: The reviews identify IL22RA1 plus IL10RB as the IL-22 signaling receptor; the cited primary studies support sequential IL10RB recruitment to IL-22/IL22RA1 and cytokine-dependent receptor activation.
limitations_preserved: Preserve sequential/low-affinity IL10RB recruitment and monomeric IL-22 receptor stoichiometry; no SCI receiver claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11115847, Structure and function of interleukin-22 and other members of the interleukin-10 family; PMCID:PMC6529849, IL-6-family cytokine receptor review
primary_title: Interleukin-22 activates the JAK/STAT, ERK, JNK, and p38 MAP kinase pathways in a rat hepatoma cell line
decision_basis: The reviews identify STAT3 as a principal IL-22 receptor output; the cited primary studies report IL-22-dependent STAT3 phosphorylation in hepatoma cells and anti-phospho-STAT3 validation in the receptor-complex structural work.
limitations_preserved: Pathway output only; do not infer universal STAT3 dominance, terminal-TF promotion, or CNS/SCI specificity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5411326, IL-17 Signaling: The Yin and the Yang; PMCID:PMC8633656, Interleukin-17 family members in health and disease

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5411326, IL-17 Signaling: The Yin and the Yang; PMCID:PMC8633656, Interleukin-17 family members in health and disease

limitations_preserved: Preserve IL-17F homodimer and distinct affinity/coupling from IL-17A; no CNS/SCI transfer.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5411326, IL-17 Signaling: The Yin and the Yang; PMCID:PMC8633656, Interleukin-17 family members in health and disease
primary_title: The human IL-17F/IL-17A heterodimeric cytokine signals through the IL-17RA/IL-17RC receptor complex
decision_basis: The reviews identify the IL-17A/F heterodimer as signaling through IL17RA/IL17RC; cited primary studies show combined soluble-receptor blockade and IL17RC-dependent heterodimer signaling.
limitations_preserved: Preserve heterodimer composition and relative receptor affinity; no terminal-TF or CNS/SCI inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC2737409, The role of TNF superfamily members in T-cell function and diseases; PMCID:PMC2928676, Mechanisms of Costimulation
primary_title: Soluble CD30 binds to CD153 with high affinity and blocks transmembrane signaling by CD30
decision_basis: The reviews identify CD30L/CD30 as a TNFSF/TNFRSF interaction; cited primary studies show high-affinity CD30L-CD30 binding and CD30-dependent cell-death/cytokine or T-cell proliferative responses.
